category: tunnel (hosted): VPN with residential and data center exit addresses run by independent node operators
tier: Plus, 2 years (Basic and Pro priced alongside)

free_tier.stated: No free plan. The pricing page shows, per 2-year term, Basic '$59.77', Plus '$54.94' and Pro '$93.37'; the monthly plan starts at '$12.99/mo' per the FAQ. A 1-year term is named in the page's term toggle ('Monthly1-Year2-Year') but its price is not in the page read: unverified: the 1-year price is behind the term toggle.
free_tier.notes: The visible default term is 2 years; every plan card lists a 30-day money-back guarantee. Plus is the cheapest plan that lists '7,500+ residential IPs' and 10 devices.

retention.stated: not applicable: a tunnel, not stored bytes

egress.terms: Unlimited data: 'Mysterium VPN is a subscription service with fixed monthly or yearly plans and unlimited data. You don't pay per GB.' The help center adds that the service has no service limitations, no data caps and no speed reductions, with fair-usage guidelines.

interface_detail: A tunnel through apps (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android, browser extensions, routers). Protocols: WireGuard and OpenVPN (OpenVPN not on Android). UDP: the help center describes WireGuard as UDP-based and its OpenVPN option as TCP. Port forwarding: not offered ('Mysterium VPN doesn’t offer port forwarding'). SOCKS5: unverified: no page read states a SOCKS5 endpoint for the consumer VPN. Obfuscation: unverified: none is stated; OpenVPN over TCP is offered for restricted networks. BitTorrent: unverified: no first-party page read states a rule.
tooling: The vendor's apps; a login with an emailed magic link. No public API for the consumer VPN is documented in the pages read.
chaining: A tunnel whose exits are labelled residential (Plus and Pro) or data center (Basic) by the vendor; the upstream sees a node operator's address, so reachability and speed depend on the individual node.

limits.value: none published: 'unlimited data. You don't pay per GB.'

exits are home connections of independent node operators ('Our 7,500+ residential IPs come from independent node operators who explicitly agreed to take part'), so speed and availability depend on the node chosen

limits_note: Concurrent devices are capped by plan: 6 on Basic, 10 on Plus, 15 on Pro (help center); the vocabulary has no kind for it.
binding_note: No byte quota or request rate is published; the decisive uncertainty is the class of the exit addresses, which is a vendor claim for the plans and is not a limit kind.

identity_cost.detail: An email address is the login and there is no password: 'MysteriumVPN does not use passwords for logging in, instead it requires an email address and access to the respective inboxes'; the magic link expires in 30 minutes. Payment: major cards, cryptocurrencies, in-app purchases, PayPal, Apple Pay and Google Pay.

reliability_note: Exits are home connections run by independent node operators, so a given node can go offline or slow; the vendor's help center says its OpenVPN option over TCP is the fallback where WireGuard (UDP) is blocked.
confidence_note: Documented for price, protocols, UDP, port forwarding and sign-up. The residential claim is a vendor claim ('7,500+ residential IPs from real people in 100+ countries') and is not measured against an address registry. The 1-year price is unverified.
price_per_tb_month: USD 54.94 billed every 2 years for Plus (USD 59.77 for Basic); a subscription price, not a per-TB price
notes: Cheapest listed price: Plus at '$54.94 billed every 2 years' ('$2.29/MO'), Basic at '$59.77 billed every 2 years'. The 1-year price is unverified: the term toggle is not rendered in the page read.
